auxiliary_material: Chemical properties of inosine (molecular weight 268.23 g/mol, stability at neutral pH, solubility).
General role of inosine in gut homeostasis (epithelial barrier integrity, tight-junction protein expression, suppression of proinflammatory cytokines in colitis models).
Challenges in therapeutic application of inosine-producing probiotics (strain selection, colonization stability, safety in immunocompromised individuals, regulatory obstacles).
Mention that short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) have been extensively studied compared to purine metabolites, but no specific SCFA concentration data is provided in this text.
Note that large-scale metabolomic studies in IBD patients link baseline serum purine metabolites to disease severity but do not resolve compartment-specific dynamics or ICI response.
outline_action: ["Use this review to establish the mechanistic rationale for inosine's role in ICI modulation (A2A receptor, T cell metabolism) in the background section.", 'Cite the explicit statements regarding the absence of human spatial/temporal concentration data to justify the need for the proposed gap analysis.', 'Retrieve and examine the original full texts of references [47] (clinical trial), [33], and [35] (metabolomic studies) to verify if paired concentration data exists but was not summarized in this review.', 'Search for independent prospective metabolomic cohorts (e.g., Gopalakrishnan, Routy, or similar ICI-microbiome studies) that may report absolute inosine or SCFA levels in paired samples.', 'Differentiate between interventional inosine supplementation data and observational baseline concentration data when synthesizing evidence for the review.']
remaining_gap: ['Absolute concentrations (μmol/g or μM) of inosine in human tumor tissue from ICI-treated patients.', 'Paired serum and stool concentrations of inosine or specific SCFAs from the same ICI-treated solid tumor patients.', 'Statistical correlation between these specific physiological concentrations and clinical ICI response (e.g., ORR, PFS, OS) in prospective human cohorts.', 'CRC-specific outcomes from the cited Phase-2 trial [47], as this review states they were not reported separately.', 'Human validation of the spatial redistribution hypothesis (luminal vs. tissue inosine gradients) during CRC progression and immunotherapy.']
useful_material: Explicit statement that human studies reporting spatial redistribution of inosine across intestinal compartments are currently missing, with most data derived from bulk metabolomic analysis.
Statement that no human studies have longitudinally tracked inosine levels or purine metabolic flux from colitis through dysplasia to established CRC.

Reference to a Phase-2 clinical trial (n=172 mixed solid tumors) evaluating inosine (0.2 g orally three times/day) as an adjunct to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and chemotherapy, noting mild efficacy enhancement but lacking separate CRC-specific reporting (n=10 within digestive system group n=55).

Mechanistic evidence from preclinical models (germ-free mice, MC38/CT26 cells) showing microbial inosine (e.g., from Bifidobacterium pseudolongum) enhances ICI efficacy via A2A receptor-dependent T cell activation and IFN-γ release.

Description of inosine's dual role: promoting anti-tumor immunity (Th1 differentiation, M1 macrophage polarization) versus supporting tumor metabolism (alternative carbon source, EMT promotion via LACC1 enzyme).
Identification of specific inosine-producing taxa (Bifidobacterium pseudolongum, Lactobacillus johnsonii/reuteri) and host enzymes (ADA, LACC1) regulating inosine availability.
